title: Letting Armstrong sleep rather than make a Washington broadcast
summary: On a one-nighter run in Washington Randolph refused to wake Armstrong for a broadcast, angering Joe Glaser and Armstrong's wife Alpha.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I never will forget Louie -- we just got into a place in Washington, Washington, D.C., and Joe Glaser says, 'We're going to broadcast,' and I said, 'Louie just got in he's got his cot down, and he's and (unintelligible) going to sleep.' He said, 'Well, he'll have to get up because we're going to broad --' I said, 'No, Louie got to have his rest. The man has got to have his rest. The man is tired. Louie is not going to broadcast.' That made Joe mad and made his wife mad -- not Lucille now, this was Alpha -- this was the other girl.
She got mad -- Alpha got mad because I was telling Louie what to do. But, see, I was looking out for the man's health. And we was -- those one-nighters was
We was playing those one-nighters, wasn't getting a chance to sleep. So, I didn't wake him up, told them don't bother Louie, (unintelligible) let him sleep.
